31	I have a complete picture. Here is my full report on the tmux URL-opening feature.
32	
33	## Summary
34	
35	`prefix + u` opens an fzf popup listing every URL in the current pane; selecting one opens it in the browser. It is powered by the third-party TPM plugin **`joshmedeski/tmux-fzf-url`** (a fork of `wenxuangm/tmux-fzf-url`). There is **no custom script** in this repo for it — the config is a single `@plugin` line using all plugin defaults. A separate, complementary feature (`tmux-open`, copy-mode `o`) also opens URLs.
36	
37	Note the capital/lowercase split: `prefix + u` (lowercase) is the URL picker; `prefix + U` (uppercase) is an unrelated "CLI tools" picker via `tv tools`.
38	
39	## 1. The keybinding
40	
41	The binding is **not** written explicitly in this repo's config — it is registered by the plugin itself, which defaults to `u`. This repo does not override `@fzf-url-bind`, so the effective binding is `prefix + u`.
42	
43	- Plugin declaration: `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/tmux/common.conf.tmpl:36-37`
44	  ```
45	  # URL picker: prefix + u opens fzf popup with all URLs in the pane
46	  set -g @plugin 'joshmedeski/tmux-fzf-url'
47	  ```
48	- The actual `bind-key` is created at runtime by the plugin's loader, `/Users/david/.tmux/plugins/tmux-fzf-url/fzf-url.tmux` (last line):
49	  ```
50	  key="$(tmux_get '@fzf-url-bind' 'u')"
51	  ...
52	  tmux bind-key "$key" run -b "$SCRIPT_DIR/fzf-url.sh '$extra_filter' $history_limit";
53	  ```
54	  Since `@fzf-url-bind` is unset in this repo, `key` = `u`.
55	
56	I confirmed there is no `bind-key u` (lowercase) and no `@fzf-url-*` override anywhere in `dot_config/tmux/`. The only `u`-family binding in `keybindings.conf.tmpl` is the uppercase `U` at line 434 (`tv tools`, a different feature).
57	
58	## 2. Mechanism & installation
59	
60	- **Type:** third-party tmux plugin, `joshmedeski/tmux-fzf-url` (GitHub repo `joshmedeski/tmux-fzf-url`; original author Wenxuan `wenxuangm`, per the header in `fzf-url.tmux`).
61	- **Install path:** TPM (Tmux Plugin Manager).
62	  - TPM itself is cloned by chezmoi external: `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl:129` → clones `https://github.com/tmux-plugins/tpm.git` into `~/.tmux/plugins/tpm`.
63	  - TPM is run at the end of the tmux config: `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/tmux/tmux.conf:26` → `run 'PATH="/opt/homebrew/opt/coreutils/libexec/gnubin:$PATH" ~/.tmux/plugins/tpm/tpm'` (macOS prepends GNU coreutils for plugins expecting GNU utils).
64	  - Plugins are populated on first setup by Ansible: `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml:4178-4200` ("Install tmux plugins via TPM", runs `~/.tmux/plugins/tpm/bin/install_plugins`, guarded by a `~/.tmux/plugins/.ansible-installed` sentinel). Manual fallback is `prefix + I` inside tmux.
65	  - Installed on this host at `/Users/david/.tmux/plugins/tmux-fzf-url/` (cloned 21 Apr).
66	
67	## 3. How URLs are extracted and opened (the picker)
68	
69	The worker script is `/Users/david/.tmux/plugins/tmux-fzf-url/fzf-url.sh`. Because this repo sets no options, it runs with defaults: `history_limit='screen'` and no extra filter.
70	
71	Flow:
72	1. **Capture pane content** — default `limit=screen` → `content="$(tmux capture-pane -J -p)"` (visible screen only; a numeric `@fzf-url-history-limit` would instead capture `-S -<N>` lines of scrollback).
73	2. **Extract candidates** via multiple `grep -oE` passes over the captured text:
74	   - `urls`: `(https?|ftp|file):/?//...`
75	   - `wwws`: bare `www.` hosts, prefixed with `http://`
76	   - `ips`: `d.d.d.d(:port)(/path)`, prefixed with `http://`
77	   - `gits`: `git@...` SSH remotes rewritten to `https://`
78	   - `gh`: quoted `owner/repo` strings rewritten to `https://github.com/...`
79	   - `npm`: `import "pkg"` statements rewritten to `https://npmjs.com/package/...`
80	   - `extras`: only if `@fzf-url-extra-filter` is set (it is not here)
81	3. **Dedupe & number**: `printf ... | grep -v '^$' | sort -u | nl -w3 -s '  '`. If empty → `tmux display 'tmux-fzf-url: no URLs found'` and exit.
82	4. **Pick**: `fzf_filter` runs `fzf-tmux -d 35% -m -0 --no-preview --no-border` (default `@fzf-url-fzf-options`). `-m` = multi-select, `-0` = exit if no matches.
83	5. **Open**: the awk-extracted URL(s) are passed to `open_url`, with a log at `/tmp/tmux-$(id -u)-fzf-url.log`.
84	
85	The exact opener:
86	```
87	open_url() {
88	    if hash xdg-open &>/dev/null; then
89	        nohup xdg-open "$@"
90	    elif hash open &>/dev/null; then
91	        nohup open "$@"
92	    elif [[ -n $BROWSER ]]; then
93	        nohup "$BROWSER" "$@"
94	    fi
95	}
96	```
97	
98	## 4. Related scripts
99	
100	No repo-managed script implements this — the extraction/opening lives entirely in the vendored plugin (`~/.tmux/plugins/tmux-fzf-url/fzf-url.sh` and `fzf-url.tmux`), installed via TPM as above. The many scripts under `dot_config/tmux/` (menus, sesh pickers, etc.) are unrelated.
101	
102	## 5. Cross-platform open handling
103	
104	Handled inside the plugin's `open_url` (above): it prefers **`xdg-open`** (Linux) if present, else **`open`** (macOS), else falls back to **`$BROWSER`**. On macOS `xdg-open` is normally absent, so `open` is used. Note the order means that if `xdg-open` exists (e.g. installed on macOS via coreutils/ports), it would win over `open`. Each launch is wrapped in `nohup` so it detaches from tmux.
105

108	Multiple docs describe it (English + zh-TW mirrors):

115	
116	## Bonus: the complementary copy-mode opener (tmux-open)
117	
118	Also relevant to "opening URLs from tmux" — `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/tmux/common.conf.tmpl:39-41`:

121	set -g @plugin 'tmux-plugins/tmux-open'

166	# herdr — full findings
167	
168	## 1. What herdr is + how it's installed
169	
170	**herdr is a Rust terminal multiplexer with built-in AI coding-agent awareness** (tracks per-pane agent state: idle / working / blocked / done). Same niche as tmux/zellij, but mouse-first and agent-native. In this repo it's a **trial tool that coexists with tmux** (you run one or the other, never nested by default).
171	
172	- **Upstream repo:** `https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr` (confirmed by the GitHub API URL in the ansible install task, `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml:4673`: `https://api.github.com/repos/ogulcancelik/herdr/releases/latest`).
173	- **Docs site:** `https://herdr.dev/docs/` — config schema at `https://herdr.dev/docs/configuration/`.
174	- **Plugin ecosystem:** `cloudmanic/herdr-plus` (`https://github.com/cloudmanic/herdr-plus`) adds "Projects" + "Quick Actions".
175	- **Hierarchy:** Session → Workspace → Tab → Pane (one level deeper than tmux).
176	
177	**Install** (`dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml`):
178	- macOS: Homebrew formula `herdr` (homebrew-core), listed in the brew block at line 89.
179	- Linux/Debian: GitHub release single static binary `herdr-linux-{x86_64,aarch64}` → `~/.local/bin/herdr` (install block starts at line 4628; the `--- herdr ---` comment). No tarball/unarchive.
180	- herdr-plus plugin: `herdr plugin install cloudmanic/herdr-plus --yes` (block at line 4713).
181	
182	## 2. Config file — exact source paths

189	| Managed body (the actual config content) | `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml` |
190	
191	**Helper scripts** in `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/herdr/`:

193	- `executable_review-mark.sh` → review-pending ⭐ flag toggler
194	- `executable_new-tab-at-space-root.sh` → new tab at workspace root

199	
200	## 3. Config schema / tables
201	
202	The managed body (`.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml`) defines these tables. The overlay **enforces** `[theme]`, `[ui]`, `[terminal]`, `[keys]` on every apply and **preserves** everything herdr writes back at runtime (`onboarding`, `[session]`, `[remote]`, `[update]`, `[experimental]`).
203	
204	- `[theme]` — `name`, `auto_switch`, `light_name`, `dark_name`
205	- `[ui]` — `mouse_capture`, `pane_borders`, `pane_gaps`, `confirm_close`, `show_agent_labels_on_pane_borders`
206	- `[terminal]` — `shell_mode`, `new_cwd`
207	- `[keys]` — **rebinds of built-in actions** + repeated **`[[keys.command]]`** array-of-tables for custom bindings
208	- `[session]` — `resume_agents_on_restore` (runtime-owned)
209	- `[remote]` — `manage_ssh_config` (runtime-owned)
210	
211	Prefix is `ctrl+b` (herdr default = tmux default). **Yes, herdr has full keybinding support**, two flavors: rebinding fixed built-in actions, and defining custom command bindings that run arbitrary shell (`type = "pane"`, plus `plugin_action`). It has a first-class notion of **panes and captured pane output** (`herdr pane read`), and opening things (via custom commands → `x open`).
212	
213	## 4. herdr keybinding format — this is what matters for the URL picker
214	
215	### Built-in action rebinds (fixed action set, value is a key or array of keys)
216	```toml
217	[keys]
218	split_vertical = ["prefix+|", "prefix+%"]
219	reload_config = "prefix+shift+r"
220	switch_workspace = "prefix+ctrl+1..9"   # "N..M" indexed-range form
221	navigate_workspace_down = ["j", "down"]
222	```
223	
224	### Custom command panes — `[[keys.command]]` array-of-tables (the URL-picker vehicle)
225	This is herdr's analog of `tmux display-popup -E`. `type = "pane"` opens a temporary pane that closes when the command exits. The command runs from the focused pane's cwd and receives env vars `$HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`, `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID`, `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD`.
226	
227	Exact shape (verbatim examples from the current config):
228	```toml
229	[[keys.command]]
230	key = "prefix+G"
231	type = "pane"
232	command = "lazygit"
233	description = "lazygit (popup pane)"
234	
235	[[keys.command]]
236	key = "prefix+U"
237	type = "pane"
238	command = "tv tools"
239	description = "CLI tools launcher (tv tools)"
240	
241	[[keys.command]]
242	key = "prefix+m"
243	type = "pane"
244	command = "~/.config/herdr/review-mark.sh toggle \"$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID\""
245	description = "toggle review-pending flag (⭐) on the current pane"
246	```
247	
248	`plugin_action` type (herdr-plus):
249	```toml
250	[[keys.command]]
251	key = "prefix+y"
252	type = "plugin_action"
253	command = "cloudmanic.herdr-plus.quick-actions"
254	description = "herdr-plus: Quick Actions"
255	```
256	
257	### Quick Action TOML format (herdr-plus, one file per action)
258	Types: `command`, `form`, `select`. Templating: `{{.Value}}`, `{{.WorkDir}}`, filters like `{{.Value | urlquery}}`.
259	```toml
260	name = "Search Google"
261	type = "form"
262	command = "x open 'https://www.google.com/search?q={{.Value | urlquery}}'"
263	[form]
264	prompt = "Search Google for"
265	placeholder = "e.g. herdr terminal multiplexer"
266	```
267	
268	### Key-syntax gotchas (documented in the config comments)
269	- Uppercase letter = `prefix+shift+<letter>`. herdr reserves `shift+H/J/K/L` (swap-pane), `shift+g`, `shift+t`.
270	- `prefix+shift+<digit>` does NOT work under the Kitty keyboard protocol (shift+1 emits `!`). Use `ctrl+digit` / `alt+digit` for indexed jumps.
271	- Validate any edit with `herdr server reload-config` — an empty `diagnostics` array + `"status":"applied"` means no keybind collisions.
272	
273	## 5. modify_ overlay mechanism (`docs/tools/herdr.md` "Config management" + CLAUDE.md line 183)
274	
275	`dot_config/herdr/modify_config.toml.tmpl` is a POSIX-sh script. chezmoi pipes the live target into stdin; the script prints the new file to stdout. Merge model:
276	- Base = the managed template `.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml` (pulled in via `{{ template "herdr/config.toml" . }}` written to a temp file through a heredoc redirect — done that way because the config contains a lone backtick in `key = "prefix+\`"` that breaks `$(...)` capture).
277	- For every top-level key in the live file NOT in `{theme, ui, terminal, keys}`, copy it into the base (preserves onboarding/session/remote/update/experimental writeback).
278	- Managed tables win wholesale (in-app theme/label overrides are re-asserted).
279	- Runs in Python via `uv run --no-project --with tomlkit --python '>=3.11'` (tomlkit round-trips comments + the `[[keys.command]]` array-of-tables). Degrades to system `python3`, then to emitting the raw template. Read side uses stdlib `tomllib`/`tomli`.
280	- **To manage a new key you edit `.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml`** (NOT the modify_ script). CLAUDE.md warns: never `chezmoi add` a `modify_` target.
281	
282	Note: `docs/tools/agent-overlays.md` does not exist; the relevant docs are `docs/tools/herdr.md` and `docs/tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md` (CLAUDE.md line 183 summarizes the `modify_` prefix behavior).
283	
284	## 6. Directly relevant to "quickly open URLs like tmux's picker"
285	
286	### The tmux model the user is copying
287	`dot_config/tmux/common.conf.tmpl:36-37`: `prefix + u` → plugin `joshmedeski/tmux-fzf-url` (TPM-installed) opens an fzf popup listing every URL in the pane; selecting one opens it. Also `tmux-plugins/tmux-open` (`o` in copy-mode opens highlighted URL). Documented in `dot_config/tmux/cheatsheet.md:29`.
288	
289	### There is currently NO herdr URL picker
290	Grepping the herdr config, helpers, and tv channels found zero URL-picker binding. `prefix+u` (lowercase) is **free** in herdr — the config only binds `prefix+U` (shift+u) to `tv tools` (`.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml:130-134`). So lowercase `prefix+u` is available and matches tmux muscle memory.
291	
292	### The building blocks to implement it (all already present in the repo)
293	1. **Extract pane text** (the URL source): `herdr pane read <pane> --source visible|recent --format text` — used in `dot_config/herdr/executable_pane-copy.sh:132`. `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID` gives the focused pane inside a `[[keys.command]]`; fall back to `herdr pane current | jq -r '.result.pane.pane_id'` (pattern at pane-copy.sh:76-78).
294	2. **Pick a URL**: pipe extracted URLs through `fzf` (available) or a `tv` channel — same command-pane popup mechanism already used for `tv tools`/`lazygit`.
295	3. **Open cross-platform**: `x open <url>` — the repo's own opener (wslview / open / xdg-open), already used by every URL Quick Action (`github.toml`, `google.toml`, etc.).
296	
297	### The natural implementation shape (a `[[keys.command]]` in `.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml`)
298	```toml
299	[[keys.command]]
300	key = "prefix+u"
301	type = "pane"
302	command = "~/.config/herdr/url-pick.sh \"$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID\""
303	description = "URL picker — open a URL from the pane (fzf)"
304	```
305	where a new `dot_config/herdr/executable_url-pick.sh` would `herdr pane read` → grep URLs → `fzf` → `x open`. This mirrors the existing `pane-copy.sh` helper exactly (same `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID` handling, same `herdr pane read` call, same `x` absolute-path fallback for command panes that run via `sh -c` without the interactive PATH). Alternatively it can be added purely as a herdr-plus Quick Action TOML, but the keybinding-pane route matches the tmux `prefix+u` UX one-to-one.
306

667	/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/tmux/cheatsheet.md:175:**Clean quit**: "Kill session & exit", "Kill all sessions (clean)", `prefix + M-Q`, and `tmux-kill-clean` clear tmux-resurrect's `last` symlink so tmux-continuum does NOT auto-restore the just-closed sessions on the next tmux start. `tmux-forget-last` / "Forget auto-restore" clears only that symlink and leaves the server running. Other kill paths (`kill-pane`, `kill-window`, plain `kill-session` when other sessions remain) do NOT touch it — the server stays alive so no restore is triggered anyway. Crash recovery is unaffected: historical snapshots stay, `prefix + Ctrl-r` can still restore manually.

5	# Set / clear / toggle a per-pane "review-pending" flag on a herdr pane, using
6	# herdr's per-pane custom-status metadata (`herdr pane report-metadata … --source
7	# review --custom-status …`). This is the herdr analog of tmux's
8	# `@bookmark_status` (dot_config/tmux/executable_toggle-bookmark.sh) — the
9	# problem it solves is the SAME: keep a session visibly flagged as "I still need
10	# to review this" even after the agent's own state flips to idle.
11	#
12	# Why custom-status and not agent state: it is pushed under a dedicated
13	# `--source review`, ORTHOGONAL to herdr's native agent detection. Verified: a
14	# pane can carry `custom_status:"⭐ REVIEW"` while `agent_status:"idle"` — so
15	# peeking into a done pane (which collapses it to idle) does NOT wipe the flag.
16	# Omitting --ttl-ms makes it persistent (no auto-expiry).
17	#
18	# The single source of truth for the mark IS herdr itself: `herdr pane get`
19	# surfaces the `custom_status` field, and `herdr pane list` (native JSON, NO
20	# --json flag) lets the `tv herdr-review` inbox enumerate flagged panes. No
21	# sidecar file.
22	#
23	# Usage:
24	#   review-mark.sh set    <pane_id> [glyph-text]   # default "⭐ REVIEW"
25	#   review-mark.sh clear  <pane_id>
26	#   review-mark.sh toggle <pane_id> [glyph-text]   # clear if flagged, else set
27	#
28	# Consumers: hmark/hunmark (dot_config/shell/24_herdr.sh), the prefix+m keybind
29	# (.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml), and the herdr-review tv channel's
30	# focus_clear action. Keep the marker MATCH substring ("REVIEW") in sync with
31	# that channel's jq filter (dot_config/television/cable/herdr-review.toml).
32	set -eu
33	
34	SOURCE_ID='review'
35	MATCH='REVIEW'                 # substring the tv channel filters on (glyph-agnostic)
36	DEFAULT_STATUS='⭐ REVIEW'
37	
38	usage() {
39	    printf 'usage: %s set|clear|toggle <pane_id> [glyph-text]\n' "$0" >&2
40	    exit 64
41	}
42	
43	command -v herdr >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "review-mark: herdr not found" >&2; exit 1; }
44	
45	action="${1:-}"
46	pane="${2:-}"
47	status="${3:-$DEFAULT_STATUS}"
48	
49	[ -n "$action" ] || usage
50	[ -n "$pane" ] || usage
51	
52	_set() {
53	    herdr pane report-metadata "$pane" --source "$SOURCE_ID" --custom-status "$status" >/dev/null
54	    echo "review flag set on $pane"
55	}
56	
57	_clear() {

60	}
61	
62	case "$action" in

64	    clear) _clear ;;
65	    toggle)
66	        command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "review-mark: jq is required for toggle" >&2; exit 1; }
67	        current=$(herdr pane get "$pane" 2>/dev/null \
68	            | jq -r '.result.pane.custom_status // ""' 2>/dev/null || true)
69	        case "$current" in

71	            *)          _set ;;
72	        esac ;;

26	# ── Internal helpers ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
27	
28	# Echo the workspace_id of an existing workspace whose label == $1 (else empty).
29	# Used for idempotency: re-running hvibe/hcode in a repo focuses the existing
30	# workspace instead of stacking duplicates (mirrors svibe's has-session check).
31	function _herdr_ws_by_label() {
32	    herdr workspace list 2>/dev/null \
33	        | jq -r --arg l "$1" '.result.workspaces[]? | select(.label==$l) | .workspace_id' 2>/dev/null \
34	        | head -1
35	}
36	
37	# Compose the shell command for one agent pane: specstory-wrap then on-exit-wrap.
38	# $1=agent  $2=specstory_mode(auto|never)  $3=on_exit(shell|kill|restart)
39	function _herdr_agent_cmd() {
40	    local inner
41	    inner=$(_sesh_wrap_agent "$1" "$2")
42	    _sesh_on_exit_wrap "$inner" "$3" "${1:-agent}"
43	}
44	
45	# Create a labeled tab in workspace $1 (cwd $2, label $3) and run command $4 in
46	# its root pane. `tab create` returns the new pane id at .result.root_pane.
47	# $1=workspace_id  $2=cwd  $3=label  $4=command
48	function _herdr_tool_tab() {
49	    local pane
50	    pane=$(herdr tab create --workspace "$1" --cwd "$2" --label "$3" --no-focus 2>/dev/null \
51	        | jq -r '.result.root_pane.pane_id // empty')
52	    [ -n "$pane" ] && herdr pane run "$pane" "$4" >/dev/null 2>&1
53	}
54	
55	# Resolve the target herdr session for hvibe/hcode from an optional --session
56	# value. Echoes "<name><TAB><socket_override_or_empty>". The socket field is
57	# non-empty ONLY when the caller must override HERDR_SOCKET_PATH (explicit
58	# --session); empty means "use the ambient/default socket untouched". Returns 1
59	# (with a message) when an explicit --session names a session that isn't running.
60	#
61	# A herdr server hosts multiple named sessions (default + `herdr --session NAME`),
62	# each with its own socket. The CLI has no --session flag on subcommands; the
63	# only lever is the HERDR_SOCKET_PATH env var (verified). `session list --json`
64	# is the authoritative name -> socket_path resolver.
65	function _herdr_session_target() {
66	    local want="$1" js line running socket nm
67	    js=$(herdr session list --json 2>/dev/null)
68	    if [ -n "$want" ]; then
69	        line=$(printf '%s' "$js" \
70	            | jq -r --arg n "$want" '.sessions[] | select(.name==$n) | "\(.running)\t\(.socket_path)"' 2>/dev/null \
71	            | head -1)
72	        if [ -z "$line" ]; then
73	            echo "session '$want' not found. Start it with: herdr --session $want" >&2
74	            return 1
75	        fi
76	        running=${line%%$'\t'*}
77	        socket=${line#*$'\t'}
78	        if [ "$running" != "true" ]; then
79	            echo "session '$want' is not running. Start it with: herdr --session $want" >&2
80	            return 1
81	        fi
82	        printf '%s\t%s\n' "$want" "$socket"
83	        return 0
84	    fi
85	    # No explicit --session: inside herdr use the ambient session (no override);
86	    # outside, fall back to the default session. Only the NAME matters here (for
87	    # the attach path) — socket stays empty so the ambient socket is left as-is.
88	    if [ -n "$HERDR_SOCKET_PATH" ]; then
89	        nm=$(printf '%s' "$js" \
90	            | jq -r --arg s "$HERDR_SOCKET_PATH" '.sessions[] | select(.socket_path==$s) | .name' 2>/dev/null \
91	            | head -1)
92	        printf '%s\t\n' "${nm:-default}"
93	    else
94	        printf 'default\t\n'
95	    fi
96	}
97	
98	# When hvibe/hcode run from OUTSIDE herdr, bring up a client attached to the
99	# session so the just-created/focused workspace is actually visible — the
100	# `herdr workspace focus` calls only move an ALREADY-attached client. Inside
101	# herdr (HERDR_ENV set) those focus calls already switched the live client, so
102	# there is nothing to do. Runs the client as a child (no exec), mirroring
103	# svibe's `tmux attach-session`. $1=session_name (default: "default").
104	function _herdr_attach_if_outside() {
105	    [ -n "$HERDR_ENV" ] && return 0
106	    local session="${1:-default}"
107	    if [ "$session" = "default" ]; then
108	        herdr
109	    else
110	        herdr session attach "$session"
111	    fi
112	}
113	
114	# ── hvibe: parametric multi-agent pack ──────────────────────────────────────
115	#
116	# A herdr "vibe" workspace: tab "agents" with N agent panes (side-by-side
117	# splits by default), tab "git" (lazygit), tab "edit" (nvim). Built directly
118	# with herdr CLI calls so pane count stays parametric.
119	#
120	# Workspace label: `vibe/<repo-basename>` (idempotent — re-running focuses it).
121	# Refuses outside a git repo (pass -p DIR, or cd into a repo).
122	#
123	# Each agent pane is specstory-wrapped (known providers) and on-exit-wrapped,
124	# exactly like `svibe` — the wrapping helpers are shared, only the layout calls
125	# differ. herdr auto-detects agent state per pane, so all N agents surface
126	# individually in the sidebar even when they share the "agents" tab.
127	#
128	# Two modes for choosing agents (same as svibe):
129	#   Homogeneous (positional):  hvibe 3 codex        → 3 panes all codex
130	#   Heterogeneous (--agents):  hvibe --agents claude,codex,opencode
131	#
132	# --tab-per-agent puts each agent in its OWN tab (own rolled-up state dot in the
133	# sidebar) instead of side-by-side splits — better for many agents, since herdr
134	# has no even-out-splits command.
135	#
136	# Usage:
137	#   hvibe                                       # auto N × claude (specstory)
138	#   hvibe 2                                     # 2× claude
139	#   hvibe 3 codex                               # 3× specstory run codex
140	#   hvibe 2 opencode                            # 2× opencode (raw)
141	#   hvibe --agents claude,codex,opencode        # 3 panes, mixed
142	#   hvibe --tab-per-agent --agents claude,codex # one tab each
143	#   hvibe --no-specstory 2 claude               # raw claude, no md auto-save
144	#   hvibe --on-exit restart 2 codex             # auto-respawn loop
145	#   hvibe -p ~/repo 2 claude                    # explicit path
146	#   hvibe --no-attach 2 claude                  # create in background
147	function herdr-vibe() {
148	    command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "hvibe: jq is required." >&2; return 1; }
149	
150	    local target="" no_attach=0 on_exit="shell" specstory_mode="auto" session_arg=""
151	    local n_agents=0 n_agents_set=0 agent_cli="claude" agents_csv="" tab_per_agent=0
152	    local min_width="${HVIBE_MIN_WIDTH:-80}"
153	    # Stagger between pane launches so agents that share a global resource at
154	    # cold start (opencode's single SQLite DB + WAL pragma) don't race. Set 0
155	    # to launch all at once. Same rationale as svibe's SVIBE_LAUNCH_STAGGER.
156	    local launch_stagger="${HVIBE_LAUNCH_STAGGER:-0.25}"
157	
158	    while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
159	        case "$1" in
160	            -p|--path)       target="$2"; shift 2 ;;
161	            --on-exit)       on_exit="$2"; shift 2 ;;
162	            --agents)        agents_csv="$2"; shift 2 ;;
163	            --session)       session_arg="$2"; shift 2 ;;
164	            --min-width)     min_width="$2"; shift 2 ;;
165	            --tab-per-agent) tab_per_agent=1; shift ;;
166	            --no-specstory)  specstory_mode="never"; shift ;;
167	            --specstory)     specstory_mode="auto"; shift ;;
168	            --no-attach)     no_attach=1; shift ;;
169	            -h|--help)
170	                cat <<'EOF'
171	hvibe — herdr multi-agent pack (herdr analog of svibe)
172	
173	Usage:
174	  hvibe [--path DIR] [--on-exit MODE] [--no-specstory] [--no-attach]
175	        [--min-width COLS] [--tab-per-agent] [--session NAME] [N_AGENTS] [AGENT_CLI]
176	  hvibe [--path DIR] [--on-exit MODE] [--no-specstory] [--no-attach]
177	        [--min-width COLS] [--tab-per-agent] [--session NAME] --agents A1,A2,A3[,...]
178	
179	Builds a new herdr workspace `vibe/<repo>`:
180	  tab "agents" — N agent panes (side-by-side splits; each auto-detected in
181	                 the sidebar). --tab-per-agent → one tab per agent instead.
182	  tab "git"    — lazygit (falls back to `git status`)
183	  tab "edit"   — nvim
184	Idempotent: re-running in the same repo focuses the existing workspace.
185	Requires:  a git repo (pass -p DIR, or cd into one).
186	
187	Attach behavior: run from OUTSIDE herdr → attaches a client to the session so
188	the new workspace is visible; run from INSIDE herdr → just focuses it.
189	--no-attach builds in the background either way.
190	--session NAME targets a running herdr session (default: the current session
191	when inside herdr, else the default session). Start a session first with
192	`herdr --session NAME`.
193	
194	Two modes for choosing agents:
195	  Homogeneous:    hvibe 3 codex → 3 panes all codex
196	  Heterogeneous:  hvibe --agents claude,codex,opencode  (list length = panes)
197	
198	Agent wrapping (auto, opt out with --no-specstory):
199	  claude / codex / cursor / droid / gemini  → `specstory run <agent>`
200	  opencode (and other unknown CLIs)         → raw passthrough
201	
202	--on-exit MODE (per pane, on Ctrl+C / clean exit):
203	  shell (default) — drop to a shell with a re-run hint
204	  kill            — let the pane close
205	  restart         — auto-respawn in a loop
206	
207	--min-width COLS (default $HVIBE_MIN_WIDTH, else 80) auto-picks N when omitted:
208	  N = clamp(term_width / min-width, 1, 6)
209	$HVIBE_LAUNCH_STAGGER (seconds, default 0.25) delays each pane launch.
210	
211	Examples:
212	  hvibe                                       # auto N × claude
213	  hvibe 3 codex                               # 3× codex
214	  hvibe --agents claude,codex,opencode        # 3 panes, mixed
215	  hvibe --tab-per-agent --agents claude,codex # one tab each
216	  hvibe --no-specstory 2 claude               # raw claude
217	EOF
218	                return 0 ;;
219	            -*)              echo "hvibe: unknown flag $1" >&2; return 1 ;;
220	            *)               break ;;
221	        esac
222	    done
223	
224	    if ! [[ "$min_width" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || (( min_width < 1 )); then
225	        echo "hvibe: --min-width must be a positive integer (got: $min_width)" >&2
226	        return 1
227	    fi
228	    if ! [[ "$launch_stagger" =~ ^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?$ ]]; then
229	        echo "hvibe: HVIBE_LAUNCH_STAGGER must be a non-negative number (got: $launch_stagger)" >&2
230	        return 1
231	    fi
232	
233	    local term_width="${COLUMNS:-$(tput cols 2>/dev/null || echo 200)}"
234	
235	    # Build the agents array (same two paths as svibe; mixing is rejected).
236	    local -a agents
237	    agents=()
238	    if [ -n "$agents_csv" ]; then
239	        if [ $# -gt 0 ]; then
240	            echo "hvibe: cannot combine --agents with positional N_AGENTS/AGENT_CLI." >&2
241	            return 1
242	        fi
243	        local tok
244	        while IFS= read -r tok; do
245	            tok="${tok## }"; tok="${tok%% }"
246	            [ -n "$tok" ] && agents+=( "$tok" )
247	        done < <(printf '%s\n' "$agents_csv" | tr ',' '\n')
248	        if [ "${#agents[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
249	            echo "hvibe: --agents list is empty." >&2
250	            return 1
251	        fi
252	    else
253	        if [ $# -gt 0 ] && [[ "$1" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
254	            n_agents="$1"; n_agents_set=1; shift
255	        fi
256	        [ $# -gt 0 ] && agent_cli="$1"
257	        # Auto-pick N from terminal width. Clamp [1,6] (lower than svibe's 12:
258	        # herdr right-splits nest, so many panes get cramped — use
259	        # --tab-per-agent for more).
260	        if [ "$n_agents_set" -eq 0 ]; then
261	            n_agents=$(( term_width / min_width ))
262	            (( n_agents < 1 )) && n_agents=1
263	            (( n_agents > 6 )) && n_agents=6
264	        fi
265	        local k
266	        for (( k = 0; k < n_agents; k++ )); do agents+=( "$agent_cli" ); done
267	    fi
268	
269	    case "$on_exit" in
270	        shell|kill|restart) ;;
271	        *) echo "hvibe: --on-exit must be one of: shell, kill, restart (got: $on_exit)" >&2; return 1 ;;
272	    esac
273	
274	    # Resolve git root (required, like svibe).
275	    local repo_root
276	    if [ -n "$target" ]; then
277	        repo_root=$(cd "$target" 2>/dev/null && _sesh_git_root)
278	    else
279	        repo_root=$(_sesh_git_root)
280	    fi
281	    if [ -z "$repo_root" ]; then
282	        echo "hvibe: not inside a git repo. Pass -p DIR, or cd into a repo." >&2
283	        return 1
284	    fi
285	
286	    # Fail-fast: every agent CLI must exist in PATH.
287	    local a missing=""
288	    for a in "${agents[@]}"; do
289	        command -v "$a" >/dev/null 2>&1 || missing="$missing $a"
290	    done
291	    if [ -n "$missing" ]; then
292	        echo "hvibe: agent CLI(s) not found in PATH:$missing" >&2
293	        echo "       Available: claude codex opencode cursor droid gemini (install as needed)." >&2
294	        return 1
295	    fi
296	
297	    local repo label
298	    repo=$(basename "$repo_root")
299	    label=$(_sesh_sanitize "vibe/$repo")
300	
301	    # Resolve the target herdr session (optional --session; else ambient/default).
302	    # A non-empty sess_sock means an explicit --session override — scope it with
303	    # `local -x` so child `herdr` calls see it but the user's shell is untouched.
304	    local sess_line sess_name sess_sock
305	    sess_line=$(_herdr_session_target "$session_arg") || return 1
306	    sess_name=${sess_line%%$'\t'*}
307	    sess_sock=${sess_line#*$'\t'}
308	    [ -n "$sess_sock" ] && local -x HERDR_SOCKET_PATH="$sess_sock"
309	
310	    # Idempotent: focus an existing workspace instead of duplicating.
311	    local existing
312	    existing=$(_herdr_ws_by_label "$label")
313	    if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
314	        echo "hvibe: workspace '$label' already exists ($existing) — focusing." >&2
315	        if [ "$no_attach" -ne 1 ]; then
316	            herdr workspace focus "$existing" >/dev/null 2>&1
317	            _herdr_attach_if_outside "$sess_name"
318	        fi
319	        return 0
320	    fi
321	
322	    # Create the workspace; capture the initial pane/tab (become the first agent).
323	    local ws_json ws p0 t0
324	    ws_json=$(herdr workspace create --cwd "$repo_root" --label "$label" --no-focus 2>/dev/null)
325	    ws=$(printf '%s' "$ws_json" | jq -r '.result.workspace.workspace_id // empty')
326	    p0=$(printf '%s' "$ws_json" | jq -r '.result.root_pane.pane_id // empty')
327	    t0=$(printf '%s' "$ws_json" | jq -r '.result.root_pane.tab_id // empty')
328	    if [ -z "$ws" ] || [ -z "$p0" ] || [ -z "$t0" ]; then
329	        echo "hvibe: failed to create workspace (is the herdr server running?)." >&2
330	        return 1
331	    fi
332	
333	    local first_agent="${agents[@]:0:1}"
334	    if [ "$tab_per_agent" -eq 1 ]; then
335	        # One tab per agent. Initial tab hosts the first agent (labeled by it).
336	        herdr tab rename "$t0" "$first_agent" >/dev/null 2>&1
337	        herdr pane run "$p0" "$(_herdr_agent_cmd "$first_agent" "$specstory_mode" "$on_exit")" >/dev/null 2>&1
338	        for a in "${agents[@]:1}"; do
339	            [ "$launch_stagger" != "0" ] && sleep "$launch_stagger"
340	            _herdr_tool_tab "$ws" "$repo_root" "$a" "$(_herdr_agent_cmd "$a" "$specstory_mode" "$on_exit")"
341	        done
342	    else
343	        # Side-by-side splits in one "agents" tab. Thread `prev` so each new pane
344	        # splits off the previous one → predictable left-to-right columns.
345	        herdr tab rename "$t0" agents >/dev/null 2>&1
346	        herdr pane run "$p0" "$(_herdr_agent_cmd "$first_agent" "$specstory_mode" "$on_exit")" >/dev/null 2>&1
347	        # Even columns: herdr has no `select-layout even-horizontal`, so set each
348	        # split's ratio explicitly. --ratio is the fraction KEPT by the pane
349	        # being split (the left one); the new pane gets the rest. Splitting the
350	        # rightmost pane on step m (of N-1) with ratio 1/(N-m+1) leaves every
351	        # finalized column at 1/N width.
352	        local n_total="${#agents[@]}" prev="$p0" np m=1 ratio
353	        for a in "${agents[@]:1}"; do
354	            [ "$launch_stagger" != "0" ] && sleep "$launch_stagger"
355	            ratio=$(awk "BEGIN{printf \"%.4f\", 1/($n_total-$m+1)}")
356	            np=$(herdr pane split "$prev" --direction right --ratio "$ratio" --cwd "$repo_root" --no-focus 2>/dev/null \
357	                | jq -r '.result.pane.pane_id // empty')
358	            if [ -n "$np" ]; then
359	                herdr pane run "$np" "$(_herdr_agent_cmd "$a" "$specstory_mode" "$on_exit")" >/dev/null 2>&1
360	                prev="$np"
361	            fi
362	            m=$((m+1))
363	        done
364	    fi
365	
366	    # git + edit tabs (same on-exit treatment as the agents).
367	    local git_inner git_label
368	    if command -v lazygit >/dev/null 2>&1; then git_inner="lazygit"; else git_inner="git status"; fi
369	    git_label="${git_inner%% *}"
370	    _herdr_tool_tab "$ws" "$repo_root" git  "$(_sesh_on_exit_wrap "$git_inner" "$on_exit" "$git_label")"
371	    _herdr_tool_tab "$ws" "$repo_root" edit "$(_sesh_on_exit_wrap "nvim" "$on_exit" "nvim")"
372	
373	    # Focus the workspace + agents tab unless --no-attach.
374	    if [ "$no_attach" -ne 1 ]; then
375	        herdr workspace focus "$ws" >/dev/null 2>&1
376	        herdr tab focus "$t0" >/dev/null 2>&1
377	        _herdr_attach_if_outside "$sess_name"
378	    fi
379	}
380	
381	# ── hcode: repo-scoped single-agent layout ──────────────────────────────────
382	#
383	# herdr analog of `scode`. Workspace `coding-agent/<repo>`:
384	#   tab "editor"  — nvim (left ~75%) | agent (right ~25%)
385	#   tab "monitor" — btop (or htop / top fallback)
386	# Idempotent per repo; refuses outside a git repo.
387	#
388	# Usage:
389	#   hcode                     # current repo, default agent (specstory → claude)
390	#   hcode codex               # right pane: specstory run codex
391	#   hcode opencode            # right pane: opencode (raw)
392	#   hcode --no-specstory claude
393	#   hcode --on-exit kill claude
394	#   hcode -p ~/work/foo
395	function herdr-code() {
396	    command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "hcode: jq is required." >&2; return 1; }
397	
398	    local target="" agent="" no_attach=0 on_exit="shell" specstory_mode="auto" session_arg=""
399	    while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
400	        case "$1" in
401	            -p|--path)      target="$2"; shift 2 ;;
402	            -a|--agent)     agent="$2"; shift 2 ;;
403	            --on-exit)      on_exit="$2"; shift 2 ;;
404	            --session)      session_arg="$2"; shift 2 ;;
405	            --no-specstory) specstory_mode="never"; shift ;;
406	            --specstory)    specstory_mode="auto"; shift ;;
407	            --no-attach)    no_attach=1; shift ;;
408	            --agents)
409	                echo "hcode: --agents is hvibe-only (hcode is single-agent)." >&2
410	                echo "       For multi-agent layouts: hvibe --agents '$2'" >&2
411	                return 1 ;;
412	            -h|--help)
413	                cat <<'EOF'
414	hcode — herdr single-agent coding layout (herdr analog of scode)
415	
416	Usage: hcode [--path DIR] [--agent CLI] [--on-exit MODE] [--no-specstory]
417	             [--no-attach] [--session NAME] [AGENT]
418	
419	Builds a new herdr workspace `coding-agent/<repo>`:
420	  tab "editor"  — nvim (left ~75%) | agent (right ~25%)
421	  tab "monitor" — btop (or htop / top)
422	Idempotent per repo; refuses outside a git repo.
423	
424	Attach behavior: run from OUTSIDE herdr → attaches a client to the session;
425	run from INSIDE herdr → just focuses. --no-attach builds in the background.
426	--session NAME targets a running herdr session (default: current session when
427	inside herdr, else the default session; start one with `herdr --session NAME`).
428	
429	Agent wrapping (auto, opt out with --no-specstory):
430	  claude / codex / cursor / droid / gemini  → `specstory run <agent>`
431	  opencode (and other unknown CLIs)         → raw passthrough
432	
433	--on-exit MODE (per pane): shell (default) | kill | restart
434	
435	Examples:
436	  hcode                     # default agent (specstory → claude)
437	  hcode codex               # right pane: specstory run codex
438	  hcode opencode            # right pane: opencode (raw)
439	  hcode --on-exit kill claude
440	EOF
441	                return 0 ;;
442	            -*)             echo "hcode: unknown flag $1" >&2; return 1 ;;
443	            *)              [ -z "$agent" ] && agent="$1"; shift ;;
444	        esac
445	    done
446	
447	    case "$on_exit" in
448	        shell|kill|restart) ;;
449	        *) echo "hcode: --on-exit must be one of: shell, kill, restart (got: $on_exit)" >&2; return 1 ;;
450	    esac
451	
452	    local repo_root
453	    if [ -n "$target" ]; then
454	        repo_root=$(cd "$target" 2>/dev/null && _sesh_git_root)
455	    else
456	        repo_root=$(_sesh_git_root)
457	    fi
458	    if [ -z "$repo_root" ]; then
459	        echo "hcode: not inside a git repo. Pass -p DIR, or use hvibe in any dir." >&2
460	        return 1
461	    fi
462	
463	    if [ -n "$agent" ] && ! command -v "$agent" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
464	        echo "hcode: agent CLI '$agent' not found in PATH." >&2
465	        return 1
466	    fi
467	
468	    local repo label
469	    repo=$(basename "$repo_root")
470	    label=$(_sesh_sanitize "coding-agent/$repo")
471	
472	    # Resolve target herdr session (optional --session; else ambient/default).
473	    local sess_line sess_name sess_sock
474	    sess_line=$(_herdr_session_target "$session_arg") || return 1
475	    sess_name=${sess_line%%$'\t'*}
476	    sess_sock=${sess_line#*$'\t'}
477	    [ -n "$sess_sock" ] && local -x HERDR_SOCKET_PATH="$sess_sock"
478	
479	    local existing
480	    existing=$(_herdr_ws_by_label "$label")
481	    if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
482	        echo "hcode: workspace '$label' already exists ($existing) — focusing." >&2
483	        if [ "$no_attach" -ne 1 ]; then
484	            herdr workspace focus "$existing" >/dev/null 2>&1
485	            _herdr_attach_if_outside "$sess_name"
486	        fi
487	        return 0
488	    fi
489	
490	    local ws_json ws p0 t0
491	    ws_json=$(herdr workspace create --cwd "$repo_root" --label "$label" --no-focus 2>/dev/null)
492	    ws=$(printf '%s' "$ws_json" | jq -r '.result.workspace.workspace_id // empty')

# Port tmux `prefix + u` URL picker to herdr

## Context

In tmux, `prefix + u` opens an fzf popup listing every URL in the current pane;
selecting one opens it in the browser. It is the third-party TPM plugin
[`joshmedeski/tmux-fzf-url`](https://github.com/joshmedeski/tmux-fzf-url)
(declared at `dot_config/tmux/common.conf.tmpl:37`, all defaults): capture the
visible pane → extract URLs with a stack of `grep -oE` passes → `fzf-tmux -m` →
`xdg-open`/`open`.

**herdr** (the repo's trial Rust multiplexer, coexists with tmux) has no URL
picker today. `prefix+u` (lowercase) is **free** — only `prefix+U` (`tv tools`)
is bound. herdr already ships every building block this needs:

- **Keybind vehicle** — `[[keys.command]] type="pane"` (herdr's analog of
  `tmux display-popup -E`): a real PTY that closes when the command exits, with
  `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID` in its env. Already used for `lazygit`/`btop`/`tv tools`.
- **Pane text** — `herdr pane read <pane> --source visible|recent --format text`
  (used in `dot_config/herdr/executable_pane-copy.sh:132`).
- **Cross-platform open** — `x open <url>` (wslview / open / xdg-open), already
  the opener in every herdr-plus URL Quick Action (e.g. `github.toml`).

Outcome: `prefix + u` in herdr reproduces the tmux UX 1:1 — fzf-pick a URL from
the pane and open it.

## New helper — `dot_config/herdr/executable_url-pick.sh`

POSIX `sh` + `set -eu`, matching the conventions of the sibling `pane-copy.sh`
(same `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID`→`herdr pane current` fallback, same absolute-path
`x`/opener resolution for the no-interactive-PATH `sh -c` command-pane case).
Reference implementation:

\```sh
#!/usr/bin/env sh
# ~/.config/herdr/url-pick.sh
# Source: dot_config/herdr/executable_url-pick.sh (managed by chezmoi)
#
# herdr analog of tmux's `prefix + u` (joshmedeski/tmux-fzf-url). Reads a herdr
# pane's text, extracts every URL-like token (same rewrite rules as tmux-fzf-url:
# http(s)/ftp/file, bare www., IPv4[:port], git@ SSH remotes, quoted owner/repo,
# npm imports), fuzzy-picks with fzf (multi-select), opens each choice via the
# repo's cross-platform `x open` (wslview / open / xdg-open).
#
# Runs inside a herdr `[[keys.command]] type="pane"` (a PTY that closes when this
# script exits), bound to prefix+u in .chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml.
#
# Usage: url-pick.sh [PANE_ID] [--source visible|recent]
#   PANE defaults to $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID (the keybind var), else the current
#   focused pane. --source defaults to visible (tmux-fzf-url's screen scope);
#   --source recent scans the full retained scrollback.
set -eu

usage() { printf 'usage: %s [PANE_ID] [--source visible|recent]\n' "$0" >&2; exit 64; }
command -v herdr >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "url-pick: herdr not found" >&2; exit 1; }
command -v fzf   >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "url-pick: fzf is required"  >&2; exit 1; }

# Resolve `x open` even without the interactive PATH (command panes run via sh -c).
if   command -v x >/dev/null 2>&1;         then X_BIN=x
elif [ -x "$HOME/.dotfiles/bin/x" ];       then X_BIN="$HOME/.dotfiles/bin/x"
else echo "url-pick: opener 'x' not found" >&2; exit 1
fi

pane=""; source="visible"
while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
    case "$1" in
        --source) source="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
        --source=*) source="${1#--source=}"; shift ;;
        -h|--help) usage ;;
        -*) usage ;;
        *) if [ -z "$pane" ]; then pane="$1"; shift; else usage; fi ;;
    esac
done
case "$source" in visible|recent|recent-unwrapped) ;; *) echo "url-pick: --source must be visible|recent" >&2; exit 64 ;; esac

# Default to the current focused pane when the keybind var was empty.
if [ -z "$pane" ]; then
    command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "url-pick: jq required to resolve current pane" >&2; exit 1; }
    pane=$(herdr pane current 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.result.pane.pane_id // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
fi
[ -n "$pane" ] || { echo "url-pick: could not determine a pane id" >&2; exit 1; }

content=$(herdr pane read "$pane" --source "$source" --format text 2>/dev/null) \
    || { echo "url-pick: failed to read pane $pane" >&2; exit 1; }

# Extraction — same passes/rewrites as tmux-fzf-url's fzf-url.sh, POSIX-ized
# (plain vars instead of bash arrays; `|| true` so a no-match grep doesn't trip set -e).
urls=$(printf '%s\n' "$content" | grep -oE '(https?|ftp|file):/?//[-A-Za-z0-9+&@#/%?=~_|!:,.;]*[-A-Za-z0-9+&@#/%=~_|]' || true)
wwws=$(printf '%s\n' "$content" | grep -oE '(https?://)?www\.[a-zA-Z](-?[a-zA-Z0-9])+\.[a-zA-Z]{2,}(/\S+)*' | grep -vE '^https?://' | sed 's#^#http://#' || true)
ips=$(printf  '%s\n' "$content" | grep -oE '[0-9]{1,3}(\.[0-9]{1,3}){3}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(/\S+)*' | sed 's#^#http://#' || true)
gits=$(printf '%s\n' "$content" | grep -oE '(ssh://)?git@\S*' | sed 's#:#/#g' | sed 's#^\(ssh///\)\{0,1\}git@\(.*\)$#https://\2#' || true)
gh=$(printf   '%s\n' "$content" | grep -oE "['\"]([A-Za-z0-9_-]+/[.A-Za-z0-9_-]+)['\"]" | sed "s/['\"]//g" | sed 's#^#https://github.com/#' || true)
npm=$(printf  '%s\n' "$content" | grep -oE "import[[:space:]]+[^\"';]*[\"']([^.][^\"';]*)[\"']" | sed "s/[^'\"]*['\"]\([^'\"]*\)['\"];*/\1/" | sed 's#^#https://npmjs.com/package/#' || true)

items=$(printf '%s\n' "$urls" "$wwws" "$gh" "$npm" "$ips" "$gits" | grep -v '^$' | sort -u || true)
if [ -z "$items" ]; then
    printf 'url-pick: no URLs found in pane %s (%s)\n' "$pane" "$source" >&2
    sleep 1.5   # command pane closes on exit — pause so the message is visible
    exit 0
fi

# fzf multi-select; Esc / no-match (exit 130 / 1) → clean no-op.
chosen=$(printf '%s\n' "$items" | fzf --multi --prompt='url> ' --height=100% --border --no-sort) || exit 0
[ -n "$chosen" ] || exit 0
printf '%s\n' "$chosen" | while IFS= read -r url; do
    [ -n "$url" ] && "$X_BIN" open "$url" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
done
\```

Key edge cases handled: `set -eu` vs. no-match greps (`|| true`) and fzf-cancel
(`|| exit 0`); empty `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID` → current-pane fallback; the
"no URLs" message pauses (`sleep 1.5`) because a command pane closes the instant
the script exits (tmux uses the status line instead); multi-select opens each URL.

## Keybind — `.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml`

Add next to the `prefix+U` (`tv tools`) block so the `u`/`U` pair sits together:

\```toml
# URL picker (tmux prefix+u analog): read the focused pane, fzf-pick a URL, open
# it with `x open`. Visible screen by default; url-pick.sh --source recent scans
# the full scrollback. Helper: ~/.config/herdr/url-pick.sh.
[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+u"
type = "pane"
command = "~/.config/herdr/url-pick.sh \"$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID\""
description = "URL picker — open a URL from the pane (fzf)"
\```

POSIX `sh` + `set -eu`, matching the conventions of the sibling `pane-copy.sh`
(same `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID`→`herdr pane current` fallback, same absolute-path
`x`/opener resolution for the no-interactive-PATH `sh -c` command-pane case).
Reference implementation:

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env sh
# ~/.config/herdr/url-pick.sh
# Source: dot_config/herdr/executable_url-pick.sh (managed by chezmoi)
#
# herdr analog of tmux's `prefix + u` (joshmedeski/tmux-fzf-url). Reads a herdr
# pane's text, extracts every URL-like token (same rewrite rules as tmux-fzf-url:
# http(s)/ftp/file, bare www., IPv4[:port], git@ SSH remotes, quoted owner/repo,
# npm imports), fuzzy-picks with fzf (multi-select), opens each choice via the
# repo's cross-platform `x open` (wslview / open / xdg-open).
#
# Runs inside a herdr `[[keys.command]] type="pane"` (a PTY that closes when this
# script exits), bound to prefix+u in .chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml.
#
# Usage: url-pick.sh [PANE_ID] [--source visible|recent]
#   PANE defaults to $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID (the keybind var), else the current
#   focused pane. --source defaults to visible (tmux-fzf-url's screen scope);
#   --source recent scans the full retained scrollback.
set -eu

usage() { printf 'usage: %s [PANE_ID] [--source visible|recent]\n' "$0" >&2; exit 64; }
command -v herdr >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "url-pick: herdr not found" >&2; exit 1; }
command -v fzf   >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "url-pick: fzf is required"  >&2; exit 1; }

# Resolve `x open` even without the interactive PATH (command panes run via sh -c).
if   command -v x >/dev/null 2>&1;         then X_BIN=x
elif [ -x "$HOME/.dotfiles/bin/x" ];       then X_BIN="$HOME/.dotfiles/bin/x"
else echo "url-pick: opener 'x' not found" >&2; exit 1
fi

pane=""; source="visible"
while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
    case "$1" in
        --source) source="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
        --source=*) source="${1#--source=}"; shift ;;
        -h|--help) usage ;;
        -*) usage ;;
        *) if [ -z "$pane" ]; then pane="$1"; shift; else usage; fi ;;
    esac
done
case "$source" in visible|recent|recent-unwrapped) ;; *) echo "url-pick: --source must be visible|recent" >&2; exit 64 ;; esac

# Default to the current focused pane when the keybind var was empty.
if [ -z "$pane" ]; then
    command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "url-pick: jq required to resolve current pane" >&2; exit 1; }
    pane=$(herdr pane current 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.result.pane.pane_id // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
fi
[ -n "$pane" ] || { echo "url-pick: could not determine a pane id" >&2; exit 1; }

content=$(herdr pane read "$pane" --source "$source" --format text 2>/dev/null) \
    || { echo "url-pick: failed to read pane $pane" >&2; exit 1; }

# Extraction — same passes/rewrites as tmux-fzf-url's fzf-url.sh, POSIX-ized
# (plain vars instead of bash arrays; `|| true` so a no-match grep doesn't trip set -e).
urls=$(printf '%s\n' "$content" | grep -oE '(https?|ftp|file):/?//[-A-Za-z0-9+&@#/%?=~_|!:,.;]*[-A-Za-z0-9+&@#/%=~_|]' || true)
wwws=$(printf '%s\n' "$content" | grep -oE '(https?://)?www\.[a-zA-Z](-?[a-zA-Z0-9])+\.[a-zA-Z]{2,}(/\S+)*' | grep -vE '^https?://' | sed 's#^#http://#' || true)
ips=$(printf  '%s\n' "$content" | grep -oE '[0-9]{1,3}(\.[0-9]{1,3}){3}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(/\S+)*' | sed 's#^#http://#' || true)
gits=$(printf '%s\n' "$content" | grep -oE '(ssh://)?git@\S*' | sed 's#:#/#g' | sed 's#^\(ssh///\)\{0,1\}git@\(.*\)$#https://\2#' || true)
gh=$(printf   '%s\n' "$content" | grep -oE "['\"]([A-Za-z0-9_-]+/[.A-Za-z0-9_-]+)['\"]" | sed "s/['\"]//g" | sed 's#^#https://github.com/#' || true)
npm=$(printf  '%s\n' "$content" | grep -oE "import[[:space:]]+[^\"';]*[\"']([^.][^\"';]*)[\"']" | sed "s/[^'\"]*['\"]\([^'\"]*\)['\"];*/\1/" | sed 's#^#https://npmjs.com/package/#' || true)

items=$(printf '%s\n' "$urls" "$wwws" "$gh" "$npm" "$ips" "$gits" | grep -v '^$' | sort -u || true)
if [ -z "$items" ]; then
    printf 'url-pick: no URLs found in pane %s (%s)\n' "$pane" "$source" >&2
    sleep 1.5   # command pane closes on exit — pause so the message is visible
    exit 0
fi

# fzf multi-select; Esc / no-match (exit 130 / 1) → clean no-op.
chosen=$(printf '%s\n' "$items" | fzf --multi --prompt='url> ' --height=100% --border --no-sort) || exit 0
[ -n "$chosen" ] || exit 0
printf '%s\n' "$chosen" | while IFS= read -r url; do
    [ -n "$url" ] && "$X_BIN" open "$url" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
done
```

Key edge cases handled: `set -eu` vs. no-match greps (`|| true`) and fzf-cancel
(`|| exit 0`); empty `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID` → current-pane fallback; the
"no URLs" message pauses (`sleep 1.5`) because a command pane closes the instant
the script exits (tmux uses the status line instead); multi-select opens each URL.

## Keybind — `.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml`

Add next to the `prefix+U` (`tv tools`) block so the `u`/`U` pair sits together:

```toml
# URL picker (tmux prefix+u analog): read the focused pane, fzf-pick a URL, open
# it with `x open`. Visible screen by default; url-pick.sh --source recent scans
# the full scrollback. Helper: ~/.config/herdr/url-pick.sh.
[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+u"
type = "pane"
command = "~/.config/herdr/url-pick.sh \"$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID\""
description = "URL picker — open a URL from the pane (fzf)"
```

78	## Keybindings
79	
80	Prefix is `ctrl+b` (same as tmux). Built-in actions can only be *rebound* (herdr's action set is fixed); everything else is a `[[keys.command]]` custom command. Custom commands receive `$HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`, `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID`, `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD` and run from the focused pane's cwd.
81	
82	> **Two families of herdr env vars.** The `HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_*` vars above are injected **only** into `[[keys.command]]` invocations. Every shell *running inside a herdr pane* also gets an **ambient** set: `HERDR_ENV=1`, `HERDR_PANE_ID`, `HERDR_TAB_ID`, `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID`, and `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` (the current session's socket). Scripts use `HERDR_ENV` as the "am I inside herdr?" test and inherit `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` to target the current session — that's what `hvibe`/`hcode` rely on.
83	
84	| Key | Action | Type |
85	|---|---|---|
86	| `prefix + c` / `prefix + 1..9` | new tab / switch tab | built-in default |
87	| `prefix + C` | new tab at the workspace (**space**) root dir — `prefix+c` + mouse "+" stay follow-focused-pane | command pane |
88	| `prefix + h/j/k/l` | focus pane | built-in default |
89	| `prefix + \|` / `prefix + %` · `prefix + minus` / `prefix + "` | split side-by-side / stacked (tmux muscle memory — both the intuitive key and the tmux default) | rebound (arrays) |
90	| `prefix + z` / `prefix + x` | zoom / close pane | built-in default |
91	| `prefix + w` / `prefix + g` | workspace navigator (navigate-mode: **`j`/`k`** *or* arrows to move, Enter to pick) / session navigator | built-in; `navigate_workspace_*` rebound to `j`/`k` + arrows |
92	| `prefix + ctrl + 1..9` | jump directly to **workspace** N (`switch_workspace`) | rebound (indexed) |
93	| `prefix + alt + 1..9` | jump directly to **agent** N's pane (`focus_agent`) | rebound (indexed) |
94	
95	> **Why ctrl/alt, not shift, for the indexed jumps**: under the Kitty keyboard protocol (which herdr uses) `shift+1` still carries the printable `!`, so herdr matches the symbol rather than `shift+1` — `prefix+shift+1..9` silently does nothing. `ctrl+digit` / `alt+digit` have no printable form and disambiguate cleanly.
96	| `prefix + [` | vi copy mode (`hjkl`, `w/b/e`, `{/}`, `v`, `y`) | built-in default |
97	| `prefix + q` | detach | built-in default |
98	| `prefix + ?` | keybinds help overlay — lists every active binding with labels (herdr's native which-key; manually invoked, not an auto-timeout hint) | built-in default |
99	| `prefix + ,` | rename tab | rebound (tmux muscle memory) |
100	| `prefix + shift + r` | reload config (`prefix + r` stays resize mode) | rebound |
101	| `prefix + shift + b` | new git worktree (moved off `prefix + shift + g`) | rebound |
102	| `prefix + G` | lazygit | command pane |
103	| `prefix + M` | btop system monitor | command pane |
104	| `prefix + N` | nvtop GPU monitor | command pane |
105	| `prefix + U` | `tv tools` (CLI launcher) | command pane |
106	| `prefix + T` | `tv herdr-sesh` (workspace/dir switcher) | command pane |
107	| `prefix + a` | `tv herdr-agent-panes` (live agent panes) | command pane |
108	| `prefix + f` | `tv fleet-hosts` (SSH picker) | command pane |
109	| `prefix + m` | toggle **review-pending** flag (⭐) on the current pane | command pane |
110	| `prefix + i` | `tv herdr-review` — review-pending **inbox** (flagged panes) | command pane |
111	| `prefix + P` | copy focused pane's **process info** to the clipboard | command pane |
112	| `prefix + D` | copy focused pane's **coordinate** (session>space>tab>pane) | command pane |
113	| `prefix + V` | copy focused pane's **content** (visible screen) | command pane |
114	| `prefix + S` | copy focused pane's **content** (full scrollback) | command pane |
115	| `` prefix + ` `` | scratch shell | command pane |
116	| `prefix + O` | herdr-plus **Projects** (layout launcher) | plugin action |
117	| `prefix + y` | herdr-plus **Quick Actions** | plugin action |
118	
119	> Uppercase letters resolve to `prefix+shift+<letter>`, which herdr reserves for built-ins (`shift+g` worktree, `shift+t` rename-tab, `shift+h/j/k/l` swap-pane). `prefix+G`/`prefix+T` are freed by the rebinds above; `herdr server reload-config` reports any remaining collisions in its `diagnostics`.

```text
281	## Copy focused-pane facts to the clipboard (`prefix+P/D/V/S`)
282	
283	Four one-keypress "grab this pane onto the clipboard" ops, all driven by one helper (`~/.config/herdr/pane-copy.sh` = [`dot_config/herdr/executable_pane-copy.sh`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/herdr/executable_pane-copy.sh)). It distills a herdr CLI call into human-readable text and pipes it to the repo's own [`x copy`](../shells/aliases.md) (auto-selects pbcopy / wl-copy / xclip / xsel / OSC 52; `x` is resolved by absolute-path fallback since a command-pane may run without the interactive PATH). The pane defaults to the **current focused pane** (`herdr pane current`); the keybinds pass `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID`, the Quick Actions pass `$HERDR_PLUS_PANE_ID`, and either falls through to the current-pane lookup when empty.
284	
285	| Op | Key | Quick Action | What lands on the clipboard |
286	|---|---|---|---|
287	| `process` | `prefix+P` | *Copy pane: process info* | foreground processes — `cmdline` + `pid` + `cwd` (from `herdr pane process-info`) |
288	| `coord` | `prefix+D` | *Copy pane: coordinate* | a paste-ready `session` / `workspace` / `tab` / `pane` id block + the `socket` path + a `# herdr pane get <pane>` line |
289	| `content` (visible) | `prefix+V` | *Copy pane: content (visible)* | the pane's on-screen text (`herdr pane read --source visible`) |
290	| `content` (scrollback) | `prefix+S` | *Copy pane: content (scrollback)* | the pane's full retained scrollback (`--source recent`) |
291	
292	The **coordinate** answers "which `session > space > tab > pane` is this?" in a form you can feed back to the CLI. herdr has **no `--session` flag** on the `pane`/`tab`/`workspace` subcommands — a session is targeted only via `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` — so the block includes the `socket=` line as the session selector (the session *name* is resolved by matching that socket against `herdr session list --json`).
293	
294	Both surfaces share the same helper: the `[[keys.command]]` binds in [`.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml) and the four `copy-pane-*.toml` **Quick Actions** under `dot_config/herdr/plugins/config/cloudmanic.herdr-plus/quick-actions/` (fuzzy-launched via `prefix+y`). `P/D/V/S` are uppercase (`prefix+shift+<letter>`) chosen to dodge herdr's reserved `shift+H/J/K/L` (swap-pane) and this repo's `shift+B` (new_worktree) / `shift+R` (reload) — confirm no collision with `herdr server reload-config` (empty `diagnostics`).
295	
296	## AI usage / quota status
297	
298	herdr has **no native usage/quota/token display** (the sidebar shows agent *state* only). It does expose a per-pane hook — `herdr pane report-metadata <pane> --source ID --custom-status "…" --ttl-ms N` — that a driver could push a `"Claude 62% • Codex 78%"` label into (the same hook the **Review-pending flag** section above uses — note both write the single per-pane `custom_status`). A Codex-only community plugin ([jerryfane/herdr-codex-usage-kit](https://github.com/jerryfane/herdr-codex-usage-kit)) already does this from the same `~/.codex` data [CodexBar](https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar) reads; nothing covers Claude/ChatGPT quota. Deferred — CodexBar's menu bar stays the multi-provider view. Design + options captured in [`backlog/herdr-usage-status-driver.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/backlog/herdr-usage-status-driver.md).
299	
300	## Gaps (no clean herdr equivalent)
301	
302	- **Seamless `Ctrl-hjkl` nvim↔pane navigation.** `vim-tmux-navigator` is tmux-coupled (the `is_vim` `ps`/`pane_tty` heuristic + the nvim plugin). herdr has no smart-splits equivalent — its pane focus is `prefix+h/j/k/l`, which won't pass through to nvim splits at the edge. Workaround: inside nvim use its own `<C-w>hjkl`. This is the biggest UX regression vs tmux.
303	- **OSC133 copy-mode** (`cpout` / `cpblock`, prompt-jump, last-output yank) is tmux-specific. herdr's copy mode (`prefix+[`) is vi-style but has no OSC133 prompt-boundary awareness. `cpcmd` (zsh history, multiplexer-agnostic) still works.
304	- **Decorative status-bar glyphs** (📌/🔖 as free-floating window labels): herdr has no `#{@option}` format-string interpolation, so tmux-style status-bar bookmarks don't port. *(The specific "mark-unread / review-pending ⭐" use case IS solved — see the **Review-pending flag** section above — via per-pane `custom_status` metadata; only the purely decorative status-bar glyph remains a gap.)*
305	- **Per-key pane resize.** tmux binds `prefix+H/J/K/L` (and `M-hjkl` for fine steps) to resize directly; herdr has no per-key resize — it uses a modal `resize_mode` (`prefix+r`), then `h/j/k/l`. Not exact parity, but a close analog.
306	
307	> **Not a gap:** vi copy-mode itself *is* native (`prefix+[`), and per-pane agent state is detected natively — the two things I expected to be missing turned out to be built in.
308	
309	## See also
310	
311	- [tmux setup](tmux/README.md) · [Television (tv)](tv.md) · [sesh](sesh.md) · [workmux](workmux.md)
312	- [Tool managers — where tools come from](../this_repo/tool-managers.md)
313
```

289	|---|---|---|---|
290	| `process` | `prefix+P` | *Copy pane: process info* | 前景 process——`cmdline` + `pid` + `cwd`（來自 `herdr pane process-info`） |
291	| `coord` | `prefix+D` | *Copy pane: coordinate* | 可直接貼回 CLI 的 `session` / `workspace` / `tab` / `pane` id 區塊 + `socket` 路徑 + 一行 `# herdr pane get <pane>` |
292	| `content`（可見） | `prefix+V` | *Copy pane: content (visible)* | pane 目前螢幕上的文字（`herdr pane read --source visible`） |
293	| `content`（scrollback） | `prefix+S` | *Copy pane: content (scrollback)* | pane 完整保留的 scrollback（`--source recent`） |
294	
295	**座標**回答「這是哪個 `session > space > tab > pane`?」,並以可餵回 CLI 的形式呈現。herdr 在 `pane`/`tab`/`workspace` 子命令上**沒有 `--session` 旗標**——session 只能經由 `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` 指定——所以區塊裡納入 `socket=` 那行作為 session 選擇器（session *名稱* 則是把該 socket 對 `herdr session list --json` 比對而得）。
296	
297	兩個介面共用同一支腳本:[`.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml) 的 `[[keys.command]]` 綁定,以及 `dot_config/herdr/plugins/config/cloudmanic.herdr-plus/quick-actions/` 下的四個 `copy-pane-*.toml` **Quick Actions**（用 `prefix+y` 模糊啟動）。`P/D/V/S` 是大寫（`prefix+shift+<letter>`）,刻意避開 herdr 保留的 `shift+H/J/K/L`（swap-pane）與本 repo 的 `shift+B`（new_worktree）/ `shift+R`（reload）——用 `herdr server reload-config`（`diagnostics` 為空）確認無衝突。
298	
299	## AI 用量 / 額度狀態
300	
301	herdr **沒有原生的用量/額度/token 顯示**（側欄只顯示 agent *狀態*）。它確實有一個逐 pane 的 hook——`herdr pane report-metadata <pane> --source ID --custom-status "…" --ttl-ms N`——driver 可以把 `"Claude 62% • Codex 78%"` 之類的標籤推進去（與上方 **待 review 旗標** 用的是同一個 hook——注意兩者都寫入單一的逐 pane `custom_status`）。有一個 Codex-only 的社群 plugin（[jerryfane/herdr-codex-usage-kit](https://github.com/jerryfane/herdr-codex-usage-kit)）已從 [CodexBar](https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar) 讀的同一份 `~/.codex` 資料做到這件事；但沒有東西涵蓋 Claude/ChatGPT 額度。延後——CodexBar 的選單列仍是多供應商的檢視。設計與選項記在 [`backlog/herdr-usage-status-driver.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/backlog/herdr-usage-status-driver.md)。
```
</details></tool-use>

**Your instinct about noise is exactly the hard part.** URLs self-identify with a `scheme://` marker, so regex alone is clean. So a regex-only path extractor *would* be noisy.

**The noise-killer is filesystem existence validation.** Extract path-ish candidates, then keep only the ones that actually resolve to a real file/dir — resolved against the *pane's cwd*, which both multiplexers hand you for free:

- tmux → `#{pane_current_path}`
- herdr → `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD` (keybind context)

Short answer: The program does not contain hard-coded PATH or URL regexes in this source file — those are read from extrakto.conf at runtime. Path/URL matching is performed by FilterDef objects using the "regex" (and optional "altN", "exclude", "lstrip", "rstrip") values taken from extrakto.conf. There is no filesystem existence check; deduplication and ordering behavior is implemented in this file as described below.

Quoted exact regex/string literals from the source (each quote ≤125 chars):

- "RE_WORD" definition:
  "RE_WORD = \"[^][(){}=$\\u2500-\\u27bf\\ue000-\\uf8ff \\\\t\\\\n\\\\r]+\""

- The code concatenates a leading newline before running each filter regex:

Behavioral details (paraphrased, not verbatim):

- Which regexes are used for PATH/URL/other token types:
  - The program loads filter definitions from extrakto.conf (and a user config at ~/.config/extrakto/extrakto.conf). Each enabled section provides a "regex" value and optional "alt2"..."alt9" values. Those exact strings (for path, url, word, quote, etc.) live in extrakto.conf, not in this Python file.
  - Alternate variants (if --alt is passed) come from any "altN" keys present in the same config section; the code will attempt each alt regex against the matched item and, on match, add the alt group's capture m[1] as name+N.

- How a FilterDef applies regexes:
  - For each match from re.finditer(self.regex, "\n" + text, flags=re.I) the code builds item = "".join(filter(None, m.groups())) (it concatenates the regex capture groups).
  - If a section provided lstrip/rstrip strings, item = item.lstrip(self.lstrip) and/or item = item.rstrip(self.rstrip) are applied.
  - Items shorter than the filter's min_length are discarded (min_length is taken from the global CLI --min-length when provided, otherwise from the filter's "min_length" setting or default 5).
  - If the filter has an "exclude" value and re.search(self.exclude, item, re.I) matches, the item is skipped.

- Path detection specifics (from code behavior, not a hard-coded regex here):
  - Whether something is considered a "path" depends entirely on the "path" section's "regex" in extrakto.conf. The source here does not hard-code any prefix rules (like ./ or ~/ or leading /) nor extension rules — those must be in the config regex.
  - No filesystem checks are performed (the code does not call os.path.exists or similar).

- URL detection specifics:
  - Likewise, URL detection uses the "url" section's "regex" from extrakto.conf. The source here does not embed a URL regex itself.

- Alternate variants:
  - If the CLI option --alt is used, for each match the code iterates over the section's alt list (alt2..alt9 values collected from the config) and runs re.search(altre, item) and, if matched, adds the capture group m[1] under the filter name with a numeric suffix (e.g., name2).

- Deduplication and ordering:
  - All results are appended to res in the sequence produced.
  - If the --reverse flag is passed, res.reverse() is called before printing.
  - Duplicates are removed while preserving order by iterating OrderedDict.fromkeys(res) and printing each key in that order.

- Lines and words:
  - get_lines(text, *, min_length=5, prefix_name=False) returns each input line stripped, keeping only lines with length >= min_length. If prefix_name is true it prefixes "line: " to the output lines.
  - The only word-related regex literal in this file is RE_WORD (quoted above); however the actual "word" filter's regex (if present) would come from the config.

- Error and matching flags:
  - Regex matching uses flags=re.I (case-insensitive) when calling re.finditer and re.search.

## 2. Keybind conflict — `prefix + Tab` / `C-i`

**`prefix + Tab` is FREE. extrakto's default `prefix+Tab` is safe — no remap needed.**

There is **no** tmux key-table binding of `Tab` or `C-i` anywhere in `dot_config/tmux/*.tmpl` or `*.conf`. Every `Tab`/`C-i` hit is a non-binding:

- `keybindings.conf.tmpl:395`, `executable_sesh-picker.sh:23`, `executable_smart-picker.sh:63` — all `--bind 'tab:down,btab:up'`, i.e. **fzf** internal keybindings, not tmux.
- `keybindings.conf.tmpl:186` — `--header 'Select lines to copy (Tab=multi, Enter=copy)'` (fzf header text).
- `common.conf.tmpl:137` — a comment (`Ctrl+I = TAB` explanation of extended-keys).
- Various `tab`/`Tab` strings in comments/headers about window tabs.

My targeted regex for a real binding — `^\s*bind(-key)?\s+(-[A-Za-z]\s+)*(Tab|C-i)` across `*.tmpl`/`*.conf` — returned **zero** matches. So there is no root-table (`bind -n`), copy-mode, or prefix-table binding of `Tab`/`C-i`. No `C-i` root binding exists that extrakto would shadow.

**One subtle non-conflict to be aware of (not a real collision):** `executable_menu.sh:28` uses `Tab` as a `display-menu` accelerator:
```
28	  "Last window"  Tab "last-window"
```
This is a menu-item shortcut that only fires while the `prefix + Space` popup menu is open — it is NOT a `prefix + Tab` key-table binding (there is no `bind Tab last-window` in `keybindings.conf.tmpl`; grep for `last-window` there returned nothing). It does not conflict with binding `prefix + Tab` to extrakto. The docs at `docs/keyboard-shortcuts.md:150` describe this menu accelerator as "`Last window` (Tab)".

## 3. Related existing copy/path binds — `keybindings.conf.tmpl`

All four are in the block at lines 183–220:

- **`prefix + C-y`** (line 184): `bind C-y run-shell "..."` — captures full scrollback (`capture-pane -pS -`), pipes into `fzf-tmux -p 80%,70% --multi --tac --no-sort` with header "Select lines to copy (Tab=multi, Enter=copy)", loads chosen lines into the tmux buffer + clipboard. **Line-by-line scrollback yank via fzf.**
- **`prefix + C-p`** (line 194): `bind C-p run-shell "tmux set-buffer -w \"#{session_name}:#{window_index}.#{pane_index}\" ; ..."` — copies the **current pane's path** (`session:window.pane`) to clipboard for reconnecting / telling an agent which pane to target.
- **`prefix + M-y`** (lines 202–207): `bind M-y copy-mode \; ...` — copies the **last command's OUTPUT** to clipboard (Warp-style), using OSC 133 prompt markers (`previous-prompt -o` → `begin-selection` → `next-prompt` → `copy-pipe-and-cancel`).
- **`prefix + M-i`** (lines 215–220): `bind M-i copy-mode \; ...` — copies the **last command's INPUT LINE** (prompt + typed command), also OSC 133-based (`previous-prompt` → `begin-selection` → `next-prompt -o` → copy).

Overlap assessment: extrakto (extract paths/URLs/words via fzf popup) is functionally adjacent to `C-y` (fzf line-pick) but keys don't collide — extrakto takes `Tab`, these use `C-y`/`C-p`/`M-y`/`M-i`. No key conflict; it's a complementary extractor.

The TPM block is at lines 4178–4235. The install task (lines 4200–4215):

```yaml
4200	- name: Install tmux plugins via TPM

**Sentinel mechanism:** a marker file `~/.tmux/plugins/.ansible-installed` (checked at 4185–4188 → `tpm_sentinel`; written at 4227–4234 "Mark TPM plugins as installed" via `file: state: touch`, only on success). The install task runs **only when the sentinel does NOT yet exist** (line 4203).

**Answer to your question:** On a **fresh** setup (no sentinel), `install_plugins` runs and reads the plugin list from the sourced config, so a newly-added `@plugin 'laktak/extrakto'` **is auto-installed** — no manual `prefix + I` needed. **`foreground_cwd`:** docs L37 (cwd model section):
> **Every pane has two cwds.** `cwd` = the shell's *startup* directory (fixed at spawn); `foreground_cwd` = the *live* cwd, tracked via **OSC 7** shell integration. A `cd` in the shell updates `foreground_cwd`; the startup `cwd` never changes.

Important nuance for your existence-validation: `pane-copy.sh` does NOT read `foreground_cwd` from `herdr pane get` — its `coord` action only extracts `.result.pane.{workspace_id,tab_id,pane_id}` (L100–102). A reliable fallback that IS proven in-repo: `herdr pane process-info` exposes per-process live `cwd`. From `pane-copy.sh` L87–91:
```
.result.process_info as $p
| "pane \($p.pane_id)  (shell pid \($p.shell_pid))",
  ( $p.foreground_processes[]?
    | "  \(.cmdline)  [pid \(.pid), cwd \(.cwd)]" )
```
So the resolution chain for relative paths: `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD` → (if empty) `herdr pane get <pane>` `.result.pane.foreground_cwd` (verify path) → `herdr pane process-info --pane <pane>` `.result.process_info.foreground_processes[0].cwd`.

1	#!/usr/bin/env sh
2	# ~/.config/herdr/pane-copy.sh
3	# Source: dot_config/herdr/executable_pane-copy.sh (managed by chezmoi)
4	#
5	# Copy distilled facts about a herdr pane to the system clipboard. Three targets:
6	#
7	#   process  the foreground processes running in the pane (cmdline + pid + cwd)
8	#   coord    the pane's coordinate in herdr's Session > Workspace > Tab > Pane
9	#            hierarchy, in a paste-ready form (the ids the herdr CLI accepts, plus
10	#            the socket path that selects a non-default session — there is NO
11	#            --session flag on the pane/tab/workspace subcommands)
12	#   content  the pane's terminal content — visible screen (--source visible) or
13	#            the full retained scrollback (--source recent, the default)
14	#
15	# The pane defaults to the CURRENT focused pane (`herdr pane current`); pass a
16	# pane id to target another. herdr's keybind context passes $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID
17	# and herdr-plus Quick Actions pass $HERDR_PLUS_PANE_ID — both are wired to call
18	# this, and both fall through to the current-pane lookup when empty.
19	#
20	# Clipboard sink is the repo's own `x copy` (dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_x), which
21	# auto-selects pbcopy / wl-copy / xclip / xsel / OSC 52. We resolve it by absolute
22	# path fallback because a herdr command-pane / quick-action pane may run us via
23	# `sh -c` without the interactive-shell PATH.
24	#
25	# Usage:
26	#   pane-copy.sh process [PANE_ID]
27	#   pane-copy.sh coord   [PANE_ID]
28	#   pane-copy.sh content [PANE_ID] [--source visible|recent]
29	#
30	# Consumers: the prefix+P/L/V/B keybinds (.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml) and
31	# the copy-pane-* quick actions (dot_config/herdr/plugins/config/
32	# cloudmanic.herdr-plus/quick-actions/). See docs/tools/herdr.md.
33	set -eu
34	
35	usage() {
36	    printf 'usage: %s process|coord|content [PANE_ID] [--source visible|recent]\n' "$0" >&2
37	    exit 64
38	}
39	
40	command -v herdr >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "pane-copy: herdr not found" >&2; exit 1; }
41	command -v jq    >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "pane-copy: jq is required" >&2; exit 1; }
42	
43	# Resolve the clipboard CLI (`x copy`) even without the interactive PATH.
44	if command -v x >/dev/null 2>&1; then
45	    X_BIN=x
46	elif [ -x "$HOME/.dotfiles/bin/x" ]; then
47	    X_BIN="$HOME/.dotfiles/bin/x"
48	else
49	    echo "pane-copy: clipboard tool 'x' not found" >&2
50	    exit 1
51	fi
52	
53	action="${1:-}"
54	[ -n "$action" ] || usage
55	shift
56	
57	pane=""
58	source="recent"
59	while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
60	    case "$1" in
61	        --source) source="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
62	        --source=*) source="${1#--source=}"; shift ;;
63	        -*) usage ;;
64	        *)
65	            if [ -z "$pane" ]; then
66	                pane="$1"
67	                shift
68	            else
69	                usage
70	            fi
71	            ;;
72	    esac
73	done
74	
75	# Default to the current focused pane when no id was passed (or an empty env var).
76	if [ -z "$pane" ]; then
77	    pane=$(herdr pane current 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.result.pane.pane_id // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
78	fi
79	[ -n "$pane" ] || { echo "pane-copy: could not determine a pane id" >&2; exit 1; }
80	
81	copy() { printf '%s' "$1" | "$X_BIN" copy; }
82	
83	case "$action" in
84	    process)
85	        info=$(herdr pane process-info --pane "$pane" 2>/dev/null) \
86	            || { echo "pane-copy: failed to read process info for $pane" >&2; exit 1; }
87	        text=$(printf '%s' "$info" | jq -r '
88	            .result.process_info as $p
89	            | "pane \($p.pane_id)  (shell pid \($p.shell_pid))",
90	              ( $p.foreground_processes[]?
91	                | "  \(.cmdline)  [pid \(.pid), cwd \(.cwd)]" )
92	        ')
93	        [ -n "$text" ] || text="pane $pane  (no foreground processes)"
94	        copy "$text"
95	        echo "copied process info for $pane"
96	        ;;
97	    coord)
98	        pj=$(herdr pane get "$pane" 2>/dev/null) \
99	            || { echo "pane-copy: failed to read pane $pane" >&2; exit 1; }
100	        ws=$(printf '%s' "$pj" | jq -r '.result.pane.workspace_id // empty')
101	        tb=$(printf '%s' "$pj" | jq -r '.result.pane.tab_id // empty')
102	        pn=$(printf '%s' "$pj" | jq -r '.result.pane.pane_id // empty')
103	
104	        ws_label=$(herdr workspace get "$ws" 2>/dev/null \
105	            | jq -r '.result.workspace.label // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
106	        tb_label=$(herdr tab get "$tb" 2>/dev/null \
107	            | jq -r '.result.tab.label // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
108	
109	        sock="${HERDR_SOCKET_PATH:-}"
110	        session=$(herdr session list --json 2>/dev/null \
111	            | jq -r --arg s "$sock" \
112	                'first(.sessions[]? | select(.socket_path==$s) | .name) // empty' \
113	                2>/dev/null || true)
114	        [ -n "$session" ] || session="default"
115	
116	        text=$(printf 'session=%s\nworkspace=%s%s\ntab=%s%s\npane=%s\n' \
117	            "$session" \
118	            "$ws" "${ws_label:+ ($ws_label)}" \
119	            "$tb" "${tb_label:+ ($tb_label)}" \
120	            "$pn")
121	        [ -n "$sock" ] && text=$(printf '%s\nsocket=%s' "$text" "$sock")
122	        text=$(printf '%s\n# herdr pane get %s' "$text" "$pn")
123	
124	        copy "$text"
125	        echo "copied coordinate for $pane"
126	        ;;
127	    content)
128	        case "$source" in
129	            visible|recent|recent-unwrapped) ;;
130	            *) echo "pane-copy: --source must be visible|recent|recent-unwrapped" >&2; exit 64 ;;
131	        esac
132	        body=$(herdr pane read "$pane" --source "$source" --format text 2>/dev/null) \
133	            || { echo "pane-copy: failed to read content of $pane" >&2; exit 1; }
134	        copy "$body"
135	        echo "copied $source content for $pane"
136	        ;;
137	    *) usage ;;
138	esac
139

22	# --source recent scans the full retained scrollback.
